advisory.summary: GET /Vehicle/GetSupplyRecordsForPlanRecordTemplate returned a vehicle's supply records to any authenticated user who named the vehicle's plan template id.
note: The endpoint loaded the plan template by caller-supplied id and returned
the supply records of the template's vehicle without checking the caller
could view that vehicle. So a user who owns a different vehicle reads
another user's supply records -- descriptions, part numbers, costs -- by
naming the victim's template id. v1.7.1 adds UserCanEditVehicle(.., View)
and answers 200 with a JSON "Access Denied" body carrying no records; the
owner still gets 200 with the records. Confirmed from source at both tags:
v1.7.0 SupplyController.cs has no access check, v1.7.1 adds it.
Status is 200 on BOTH builds, so a status oracle is blind to the fix --
only the planted marker distinguishes them. The owner is declared in the
same check as the positive control: its 200-with-marker proves the marker
is live and reachable on the patched build, so the attacker's marker-free
200 there is a real exclusion, not an unproven one.
LubeLogger accepts HTTP Basic against its AuthN scheme on every route when
EnableAuth is set, so each identity is a static Authorization header.
Measured by hand on both tags before this was written: the attacker gets
403 at /api/vehicle/info for the owner's vehicle (no allowed route to it)
and 200 reading a plan template of its own (its credential is valid on the
patched build), so the patched build's marker-free 200 is the fix, not a
refused credential.

checks.name: A user must not read another user's supply records via a plan template id
